actor.description: Recorded actor identity, not host-authenticated authority.

file.description: A staged file relative to the work directory. The consumer verifies its actual bytes against sha256.

relativePath.description: A slash-separated file path relative to the work directory; no absolute path, dot segment, parent traversal, drive prefix or backslash.

context.description: Supporting notes and reference files used to understand the task, separate from its inputs. Empty collections explicitly mean no extra context. Context does not grant additional execution authority.
context.title: Request context

decision.description: .works/<workId>/decisions/<id>.json: an attributed decision on an exact work revision and subject digest. Identity and authority are not authenticated by this schema.
decision.title: Decision

evidence.description: .works/<workId>/evidence/<id>.json: artifact metadata. Existence, actual digest and evidentiary relevance require separate checks.
evidence.title: Evidence

index.description: Version 1 of the proposed .works document format. A document must match exactly one kind. This contract does not migrate or reinterpret legacy session records.
index.title: Works document contract

inputs.description: The prompts and files the request asks the skill to act on. At least one prompt or file is required.
inputs.title: Request inputs

output.description: One produced output. Text is inline; commits identify a repository and full object ID; images and other files bind persisted artifacts. Output metadata alone does not prove correctness or publication.
output.title: Response output

request.description: .works/<workId>/requests/<id>.json: prompts and files to act on, with supporting context kept separate, against one work revision. This record alone grants no execution permission.
request.title: Request

response.description: .works/<workId>/responses/<id>.json: typed outputs produced for one request. Optional verification observations describe their checks separately; delivering an output is not a claim that the work is proved complete.

feedbackRound.description: Completed feedback-and-repair rounds for this request. Initial candidate is round zero; the caller maintains truthful history.

response.title: Response

work.description: .works/<id>/work.json: goal, declared scope, acceptance criteria and current lifecycle.
work.title: Work

@cli/git.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/git.purpose: Inspect or change Git repository state.

@cli/python.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/python.note: Resolve Python 3 from the active environment: python, python3, or py -3 as appropriate; record the selected executable and any launcher arguments.

@cli/shell.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/shell.note: Resolve to the session shell (PowerShell, bash or another declared shell); do not assume bash on Windows. Arguments remain separate data until encoded for that shell.
@cli/shell.purpose: Run a declared command in the active session shell.

@remote/git.bind: Explicit remote URL and observed remote commit.
@remote/git.purpose: A named Git remote of the bound repository.

@tools/fileread.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/fileread.purpose: Read declared workspace files and directories through the active session.

claude.via: Claude Code Read, Glob and Grep

@tools/print.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/print.purpose: Present text and artifacts in the conversation using the host rendering capabilities.

claude.via: the session's file and render hand-off, which displays an image or an HTML page in the conversation and falls back to the path or the URL

openai.via: the absolute path or the URL printed into the conversation, with the image inline where the client renders one

@tools/sourcewrite.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/sourcewrite.purpose: Edit files within the declared write scope through the active session.

@workspaces.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.

@workspaces/artifacts.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/artifacts.purpose: Produced files, including images, documents and other deliverables.

@workspaces/context.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/context.purpose: Supporting reference files for a request.

@workspaces/inputs.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/inputs.purpose: Files supplied as the subject of a request.

@workspaces/requests.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/requests.purpose: Requests with separate inputs and context.

@workspaces/responses.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/responses.purpose: Responses declaring produced outputs and execution status.

criteria.history: Record initial local and remote heads, approval, hooks, merge decisions, attempted effects and read-back. Each retry starts from fresh remote observation; preserve rejected attempts and never repeat an uncertain push.

items.expect: Route, changes, quality and approval evidence match digests.

onFail.instruction: Request exact missing or stale publication evidence.

items.expect: The response schema and publication outputs pass.

onFail.instruction: Repair response metadata from read-back proof only.

items.expect: The response binds this publication request and revision.
The publication receipt is present, scoped and digest-bound.

onFail.instruction: Re-read actual receipt bytes and correct metadata.

items.expect: Observations reference request criteria and publication evidence.
Existing approval covers the exact boundary, target and optional tag at the verified commit.

onFail.instruction: Request approval for the exact boundary or stop; completion proof is not approval.

items.expect: Only owned changed paths are published and required session evidence is present.

onFail.instruction: Name the dirty outside path or missing session proof; do not expand the boundary.

items.expect: Hooks pass without bypass and merge provenance follows the closed non-rebase policy.

onFail.instruction: Report the hook, conflict or post-merge gate defect; repair must produce a new verified head.

items.expect: Remote creation or advance is authorized, non-force, fast-forward and read back exactly.

onFail.instruction: Fetch and classify remote state before any further action; never force or blindly retry.

items.expect: Exactly the requested authorized annotated tag exists on the published head, or no tag exists.

onFail.instruction: Report tag mismatch; do not delete or rewrite a remote tag without separate authority.

items.expect: Git, shell and remote-read capabilities are available.

onFail.instruction: Return the missing capability; no bypass is allowed.

items.expect: Route, boundary, verified commit, remote observation and approval are supplied.

onFail.instruction: Ask for the exact missing authority or proof before mutation.

items.expect: Merge, push and tag effects have known outcomes.

onFail.instruction: Fetch local and remote refs first; never repeat a push or tag whose completion is uncertain.

criteria.stopWhen: Stop after two feedback rounds, recurring hook or ancestry failure, changed remote, missing approval, unavailable capability or uncertain unobservable effect. Never force, rebase, bypass hooks or duplicate publication effects.

purpose: Publish one approved Git boundary from the exact commit quality verified, using hooks, non-force fast-forward semantics and remote read-back proof.

request.description: Bind the verified workspace route, exact changes boundary, passing quality evidence, current remote observation and an existing approval for this boundary. An optional annotated tag must be explicitly named and authorized.
request.title: git.publish request

response.description: A done response binds the exact verified commit and a publication receipt containing approval, boundary, hooks, observed-before and read-back remote heads, publication mode and optional annotated tag.
response.title: git.publish response

scope: One approved repository boundary and target ref. It decides nothing about the change, never rebases or force-pushes, never bypasses hooks, and creates a tag only when the request explicitly authorizes that exact annotated tag.

calls.purpose: Read publication authority and producer evidence.
Read local and remote heads and ancestry.

steps.instruction: Read the request and declared route, changes, quality evidence, current remote observation and approval. Bind one exact boundary, verified commit, target ref and optional annotated tag. Confirm the approval covers every intended publication effect.
produces: Authorized publication boundary and observed remote head.

calls.purpose: Inspect tree, branches, diffs and hook configuration.

steps.instruction: Verify route, exact changed-file ownership, clean tree outside the boundary, branch policy and required original session receipts at the verified head. Run installed hooks without bypass.

reads.when: when required by the delivery chain

calls.purpose: Merge by policy and publish without force.
Rerun declared gates if a merge hunk was resolved.
Record the exact attempted effect and observed precondition.

steps.instruction: Resolve only rule-covered merge hunks inside the owned boundary, rerun named gates on a merged head, then create the approved ref or push a non-force fast-forward. Create the optional annotated tag only when explicitly authorized. Never rebase, force or bypass a hook.

writes.when: only when the approved policy merge changes the local target branch
when a publication command is attempted

calls.purpose: Fetch and read back exact remote objects.

steps.instruction: Fetch and read the remote ref and optional tag after the attempt. If completion was uncertain, this observation happens before any retry; a changed remote is never pushed blindly.

calls.purpose: Persist the publication receipt only from observed evidence.

steps.instruction: Compare authority, boundary, hooks, merge provenance, verified commit and remote read-back. Record concrete defects; do not treat a rejected or uncertain push as published.
produces: Concrete failed-criterion feedback or passing review results.

steps.instruction: Write and validate the response with actual commit and receipt outputs, observations and review results. Present a publication link only after remote read-back equals the verified commit.

validate.failurePolicy: Record the exact authority, boundary, hook, ancestry or remote defect and reassess after targeted repair. Never retry an uncertain push before fetching the remote, and never use force, rebase or hook bypass.

review.instruction: Confirm the approval names this exact boundary, target ref and optional tag, the routed checkout is verified, and the published commit is exactly the quality-verified commit.
Confirm the exact changed-file set is owned by the approved boundary, nothing dirty lies outside it, and session evidence required by the delivery chain is present at the same head.
Verify installed hooks ran without bypass. Any integration merge uses a merge commit, resolves only rule-covered owned hunks, and reruns the named gates after conflict resolution.

Confirm the target ref was created as approved or advanced fast-forward only, no force or rebase occurred, and fetch/read-back equals the published commit. A changed or uncertain remote is observed before any retry.
When requested, confirm exactly one authorized annotated tag points to the published head; otherwise confirm no tag was created.
